UserFact.title: UserFact
UserFact.description: Stores individual facts about a user to provide context for the LLM.

id.description: Unique identifier for the user fact.

userId.description: Reference to the user this fact belongs to.

fact.description: The fact about the user (e.g., 'Likes Python').

timestamp.description: Timestamp of when the fact was recorded.

relevanceScore.description: Score indicating the relevance of the fact to the current conversation. Higher score indicates greater relevance.

definition.description: Stores facts specific to each user, used to contextualize LLM prompts. Path-based ownership ensures only the user can access their own data.

params.name: userId
params.description: The unique identifier for the user.

params.name: factId
params.description: The unique identifier for the user fact.

firestore.reasoning: The Firestore structure is designed to store user facts extracted and used to contextualize LLM prompts. It leverages path-based ownership for securing user-specific data. Specifically, user facts are stored within a subcollection of each user's document. This ensures that only the user has access to their own facts, eliminating the need for complex security rules based on document content or hierarchical `get()` calls. The structure achieves Authorization Independence by isolating each user's data under their own `userId`, eliminating cross-user authorization checks. This simplifies rules and enables atomic operations. Because the data is nested under the user, QAPs are easily met by scoping `list` operations to the user's path and enforcing the schema.
